title.narrative: STAR project (Supporting Transformative Action and Resilience) of GBV Survivors and Vulnerable Community in Raya Kobo, Habru, Lasta, and Bugna Woredas of North Wollo, Amhara Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed STAR project (Supporting Transformative Action and Resilience) women-led initiative by ELiDA and sup-IP (UEWCA), is designed to address critical GBV (prevention and response) needs for 41,641 women, girls and other vulnerable communities aiming to reduce the prevalence of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and enhance the safety, well-being, and resilience of women and girls in the conflict-affected North Wollo Zone of Amhara Region, specifically within Raya Kobo, Habru, Lasta, and Bugna Woredas. As a leading women-led organization with deep operational presence in the proposed Woredas, we are uniquely positioned to implement this vital program with our implementation methodology is inherently on human right based approach centering women's, girls and disability, feminist and participatory, a community-centered approach, recognizing local community structure as vital pillars of protection and change. lt/pgtltpgtPrevention efforts begin with a rapid protection risk analysis, tailored to the specific vulnerabilities in the four Woredas, ensuring contextual relevance. Empowering communities to challenge harmful gender norms and transform attitudes. To bolster local capacity, we will conduct PFA and MHPSS training for project staff, women's affairs experts, health and legal officers, to effectively support the need communities. lt/pgtltpgtltspangtRecognizing the need for coordination, we will strengthen GBV coordination at National, subnational (Amhara), zonal (North Wollo), and Woreda levels for an efficient response system. Establishing and supporting community-based protection mechanisms will create accessible avenues for reporting. We will regularly conduct/update GBV referral pathways and service mapping within each Woreda to ensure clear access to comprehensive services. Our advocacy includes GBV prevention activism/awareness-raising, such as the 16 Days of Activism and March 8 and other community led campaigns. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtFor GBV Response, our methodology prioritizes survivor-centered care and access to justice within the target woreda by facilitate intensive GBV case management training for frontline service providers and deliver case management through compassionate and survivor centered support. Establishing and functionalizing a GBV/SEA hotline for confidential reporting and referral, offering immediate guidance. We will actively support establishing/renovating One Stop Centers (OSCs) in key Woreda locations, equipping them for comprehensive, integrated services. Rehabilitating Women's and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) will provide vital havens. Practical support includes distributing cash for protection and case management to address immediate needs and providing dignity kits for at-risk women and girls. Critically, we will empower Persons with Disability Organizations (PDOs) through capacity building, technical, and material support based on their assessed needs.lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project will significantly complement ELiDA UWCA existing similar programs, leveraging our established trust and infrastructure in Amhara specifically, ELiDA ground presence with portfolio includes a GBV Prevention and Response project funded by UNTF till Feb, 2027 in Habru, Kobo, and Raya Kobo, which has built foundational capacities and our experience from an EU-supported project in Raya Kobo (and Gulina in Afar, which phased out in April 2025), focusing on GBV prevention and response. Furthermore, building resilience to online offline violence in Amhara, Tigray and Oromia funded by GAC through Search for Common Ground, an AFD-funded Women-led in Emergency project which will run as Nov 2028, WPHF Gender responsive monitoring of the national dialogue project, AWDF-supported Women's Engagement in Peacebuilding and Social Cohesion project till Feb 2026 in Habru and Girls education project in Amhara. ELiDA will take careful attention and prioritize those locations within the target Woredas which are not yet covered by our existing programs and avoiding duplication of efforts. lt/spangtlt/pgt
